author: Albee Zhang
description:
When Zhuhai hosted its inaugural air show in November 1996, the event showcased the J-8IIM fighter, a second-generation fighter equipped with Russian radar and weapons, alongside a limited line-up of home-made aircraft.
Imported planes were the focus and Chinese audiences curiously studied the much more advanced foreign designs. They crowded around two Russian fourth-generation Su-27 fighters and were wowed as the jets performed their famous cobra manoeuvre, sharply braking in mid-air.
At the...
title: How the Zhuhai air show charted China’s path from catching up to flying high

author: Lucy Quaggin,Nayan Seth
description:
As Washington seeks to loosen China’s dominance over critical minerals, US Secretary of State Marco Rubio urged other members of the Group of 20 (G20) to strengthen supply chains and secure strategic trade routes as the group’s foreign ministers’ meeting drew to a close in Atlanta on Saturday.
Rubio said there was a “universal recognition” among the G20 members over the importance of issues like critical minerals, supply chain security and freedom of navigation.
“The first step is at least some...
title: G20 foreign ministers end Atlanta meeting without consensus on key issues

author: Nayan Seth
description:
Top diplomats from the Quadrilateral Security Dialogue, or the Quad, met in Atlanta on Saturday to finalise preparations for next month’s summit in the Philippines, just weeks before US President Donald Trump is scheduled to meet Chinese leader Xi Jinping in Shenzhen.
US Secretary of State Marco Rubio met his counterparts from India, Japan and Australia on the sidelines of the Group of 20 (G20) foreign ministers’ meeting, where they reaffirmed their commitment to a “free and open...
title: Quad diplomats finalise first leaders’ summit in two years before Trump-Xi meeting

author: Eve Qiao
description:
China is further narrowing access to a key government recruitment programme for overseas-educated graduates, limiting their pathways into the country’s civil service and party-state system.
More than a dozen provincial-level regions, including Beijing and Shanghai, opened applications for the 2027 xuandiaosheng recruitment rounds in September and October.
Xuandiaosheng, or the “selected graduates” system, is designed to select and train university graduates to become elite cadres and officials...
title: China narrows the path to elite official training scheme for citizens graduating overseas

author: Holly Chik
description:
Chinese archaeologists are set for a hi-tech turn, with the latest five-year blueprint aiming to deploy AI and deep-sea robots to trace Chinese history, decipher the origins of East Asian humans and expand the country’s cultural soft power.
Scientists will develop technologies such as remote sensing, ancient DNA analysis, underwater archaeology robots and artificial intelligence (AI) models for virtual restoration of excavated artefacts, according to the 15th five-year work plan for...
title: Chinese archaeologists set for hi-tech excavations with AI and deep-sea robots

author: Laura Zhou
description:
Chinese first lady Peng Liyuan hosted her German counterpart, Elke Buedenbender, in Beijing on Friday for a tea reception in a bid to showcase Beijing’s soft power and foster closer bilateral ties.
Peng stressed the rich cooperation with Germany in areas including education and culture, according to official news agency Xinhua.
She also expressed hope that people from the two countries would “visit each other more often, continuously deepen mutual understanding and foster closer people-to-people...
title: Soft power on display as China’s first lady Peng Liyuan hosts German counterpart

author: Gabriel Dominguez,Amber Wang
description:
America’s push for 2027 combat readiness in the Indo-Pacific is raising questions over whether a year that US military officials linked to a possible People’s Liberation Army attack on Taiwan has instead become a planning benchmark.
The preparations come despite a US intelligence assessment published in March that mainland Chinese leaders “do not currently plan” to attack Taiwan in 2027, “nor do they have a fixed timeline for achieving unification”.
General Ronald Clark, commander of US Army...
title: Is Beijing’s 2027 military milestone now a US readiness deadline over Taiwan?

author: Albee Zhang
description:
Beijing and Washington have been urged to foster a new generation of talent to bridge gaps between the countries and strengthen people-to-people exchanges amid growing frictions and concerns about a lack of China expertise in the US.
Academics and experts from the two countries gathered in Shanghai on Friday at the China-US Intergenerational Dialogue 2026. They were seeking a new crop of “bridge builders” like Henry Kissinger, the former US secretary of state who helped to engineer the historic...
title: With ‘Kissinger moment’ over, US and China urged to foster new ‘bridge builders’

author: Laura Zhou
description:
Fu Chengyu, the former chairman of leading oil giants Sinopec and China National Offshore Oil Corporation (CNOOC), is under investigation for corruption by the country’s top watchdogs.
The Communist Party’s Central Commission for Discipline Inspection (CCDI) was investigating Fu for alleged “serious violations of discipline and law”, a euphemism for corruption, state news agency Xinhua reported on Saturday, quoting a notice posted on the commission’s website.
He is “currently undergoing...
title: China places former Sinopec and CNOOC boss Fu Chengyu, 75, under corruption probe

author: Dannie Peng
description:
China’s social credit system, stereotypically imagined as an all-powerful numerical scoring project for authoritarian control, has gained notoriety in the West – although people inside the country actually feel little of its presence or practical influence.
In a government-funded study, however, a Chinese legal scholar warned that deploying artificial intelligence (AI) risked turning the rating system into a “large-scale surveillance tool”. The paper was published in the Journal of Sichuan...
title: AI could turn China’s social credit system into surveillance tool: government-funded study

author: Holly Chik
description:
China’s Ministry of Commerce has voiced firm opposition to a decision by the US Federal Communications Commission (FCC) to bar device testing in China by 2028.
“This has seriously harmed the interests of China and other trading partners, seriously undermined the stability of China-US economic and trade relations, and seriously disrupted the stability of global industrial and supply chains,” it said in a statement on Friday night.
“[We] hope the United States will face the calls of the industry,...
title: Beijing blasts US ban on device testing in China, warns of supply chain disruptions

author: Dannie Peng
description:
Prominent biologist Rao Yi is refusing to back down after Cell Press said it had found no evidence that top journal editor Steve Mao sought bribes from Chinese scientists.
In a statement published on Thursday evening, Cell Press – one of the world’s leading scientific publishers, owned by Elsevier – said its investigation had “largely concluded” and “found no evidence to support the aforementioned allegations”.
Nevertheless, Rao, a tenured chair professor at Peking University who stepped down as...
title: Mao vs Rao: Cell Press probe clears editor but Chinese biologist keeps up pressure

author: Alcott Wei
description:
Beijing promoted 10 officials to full membership of the Communist Party’s Central Committee at a major political gathering this week, where the normally routine process of filling vacancies took on new significance.
The names of the officials who have filled the vacant slots were included in a communique released at the end of the fifth plenum of the party’s 20th Central Committee on Thursday.
The event, which focused on party discipline and the fight against corruption, confirmed that 24 full...
title: Are the latest Communist Party promotions a sign of a new political trend in China?

author: Mark Magnier
description:
The film Everest: The Other Side, a collaborative US-China project that opened on Friday in 515 US cinemas and that will premiere at 700 IMAX theatres in China on November 6, starts with a majestic shot of the world’s tallest mountain. Then the music builds and more challenging weather rolls in, foreshadowing what is at stake.
The film invokes a well-trod narrative for fans of the mountaineering genre: a mix of the grit and sacrifice driving world-class climbers, along with no small amount of...
title: New Everest film hopes to nudge US-China relations into a higher altitude
